description: Enhance species JSON data with safari_scene and comic_strip fields, add scalable architecture for arbitrary species, and ensure the globe shows 'coming soon' placeholder dots for future species locations.
steps: STEP 1 - Update all 10 species JSON files in public/data/ to add safari_scene and comic_strip fields. For each species, add: (a) safari_scene object with: { biome_type: string matching habitat.type, sky_gradient: [color1, color2] for top-to-bottom sky, silhouette_color: hex for distant landscape, mid_color: hex for vegetation, foreground_color: hex for close elements, atmosphere: 'warm'|'cool'|'neutral' }. (b) comic_strip array with 6 objects, each: { panel_number: 1-6, label: string, title: string, narrative_text: string (2-3 sentences telling the story), source: string or null, source_url: string or null }. The 6 panels follow the arc: 1=Species in habitat, 2=Cultural/mythological bond, 3=Primary threat arrives, 4=Human-wildlife interaction story, 5=Conservation efforts, 6=The future outlook. Derive all text from existing data fields (habitat.description, cultural_depth, threats, conservation, cultural_significance).

STEP 2 - Update tiger.json comic_strip example: Panel 1 title 'Lord of the Forest' narrative from habitat.description first paragraph. Panel 2 title 'Sacred Guardian' from cultural_depth.india_waghoba. Panel 3 title 'Habitat Under Siege' from threats[0]. Panel 4 title 'The Sundarbans Pact' from cultural_depth.india_sundarbans. Panel 5 title 'Project Tiger' from conservation.key_programs. Panel 6 title 'A Fragile Recovery' from conservation.population_trend + estimate.

STEP 3 - Update african-elephant.json, polar-bear.json, snow-leopard.json, blue-whale.json, bornean-orangutan.json, hawksbill-turtle.json, giant-panda.json, staghorn-coral.json, amazon-river-dolphin.json with appropriate safari_scene colors and comic_strip content derived from their existing data. Each species should have biome-appropriate colors (e.g., polar-bear: icy blues/whites, african-elephant: warm savanna golds/browns, blue-whale: deep ocean blues).

STEP 4 - Update src/globe.js to support 'coming soon' markers: Add a COMING_SOON_HOTSPOTS array with 5-8 placeholder locations for future species (e.g., lat/lng for Galapagos Islands, Madagascar, Yellowstone, Great Barrier Reef outer sections, Congo Basin, Himalayas). These render as small dim dots (lower opacity, smaller size, no click interaction) on the globe. They appear in all layer modes. Add a tooltip 'Coming Soon' on hover.

STEP 5 - Update src/safari-scene.js to use the new safari_scene field from JSON data: When rendering the parallax hero, use safari_scene.sky_gradient for the sky layer CSS gradient, safari_scene.silhouette_color for the far landscape layer, safari_scene.mid_color for vegetation layers. When rendering comic strips, use the comic_strip array directly instead of generating panels from raw data. Fall back to auto-generation (FEAT-002 logic) if comic_strip field is missing for backwards compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build succeeds without errors
All 10 species JSON files in public/data/ contain a safari_scene object with biome_type, sky_gradient, silhouette_color, mid_color, foreground_color, atmosphere fields
All 10 species JSON files contain a comic_strip array with exactly 6 panel objects each having panel_number, label, title, narrative_text fields
globe.js contains a COMING_SOON_HOTSPOTS array with at least 5 placeholder locations
safari-scene.js reads safari_scene and comic_strip from species data when available
verification: Run `npm run build` in /projects/sandbox/species-on-screen and confirm exit code 0 and dist/ output

Verify JSON validity by running: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const files=['tiger','african-elephant','polar-bear','snow-leopard','blue-whale','bornean-orangutan','hawksbill-turtle','giant-panda','staghorn-coral','amazon-river-dolphin'];files.forEach(f=>{const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('public/data/'+f+'.json'));if(!d.safari_scene||!d.comic_strip||d.comic_strip.length!==6)throw new Error(f+' missing fields')});console.log('All valid')"
